reason: The observations check out; the conclusion and the fix do not. Driven at 1440 on owner-flight: .b-grab::after is inset:0 against .b-copy (.b-grab is position:static, .b-copy is position:relative), elementFromPoint at the centre of .b-away returns the span, its computed cursor is 'auto', and a click leaves every .b-grab at aria-expanded=false with activeElement BODY. Hovering it does paint .b-copy at rgba(255,255,255,0.04) and lift .b-grab to rgb(255,255,255) on a 6% plate. All true. But that is not a false promise: the cursor over the count and the tick is the plain arrow, while the cursor over the words is 'pointer' (verified: elementFromPoint over .b-title returns .b-grab, cursor 'pointer'). The pointer is told, in the one channel that states pressability, that the count is not a control. A readout that does nothing when pressed is a readout, not a defect. Worse, what the finding calls a lie is the one useful thing in the behaviour: the hover is scoped :has(.b-grab) and links the number to the words it names, which is precisely the crowded-rail problem the design already spends a leader line on - in the day state .b-away sits up to 147px from its own title. Removing pointer-events from .b-away and .b-tick, which is otherwise free (they carry no handler, and at every width they sit entirely left of the copy column - 586-670 and ~683 against copy at 710 at 1440, 20-96 against 130 at 390 - so they could never have caused, and their removal cannot reintroduce, the round-8 swallowing, which was the .b-item BOX overlapping the row above), costs that linkage and buys nothing. And the proposed fix reintroduces the round-8 defect outright. It moves the hit area back onto .b-item with inset:0 and offsets only [data-stack="follow"] rows by --push. But --push is written for ANY row whose true pixel falls above the previous row's bottom, independent of data-stack: in owner-flight, opening the last row and pressing 'Move a day earlier' ten times yields demo-audience-item-wedding at data-crowded="true", data-stack="-", --push:18px, carrying a .b-grab, its box top at 485 against the preceding row's box bottom at 490 - an armed 18px band lying across that row's Edit control, extended further left over the count lane by the same fix. The day state shows the same shape at --push up to 147px. That is one press away from the exact failure round 8 was paid to remove, and the b.css comment says why the scoping the fix proposes is unsafe: push is written by script after layout and an attribute-keyed rule falls out of step with it. Not a gate restatement - the behaviour gate iterates .tl-stage button and these are spans, and 'the whole row is the target' samples only .b-title - but a thin nit whose fix is a regression.
